_comment: Hand-written example case v2.1 — Maria Santos / Neurocysticercosis. Redesigned for granular sub-action gating and narrative unlock chains. v2.1 (P2-H09): survivable crisis via emergency_intervention, post-crisis re-arm into a second crisis, timeout fallthrough tier, OPTIMAL window widened to 150, family_alienated wired into tier scoring.

learning_objectives: Diagnostic anchoring on imaging is dangerous — follow the full clinical picture
Environmental and dietary history is as important as test results
Eosinophilia in a patient with a brain lesion should change your differential immediately
Steroids treat symptoms and destroy the patient — mechanism matters
Family members hold diagnostic keys that patients will not offer unprompted
content_boundaries: Death is possible but not gratuitous

patient.name: Maria Santos
patient.chief_complaint: Sudden speech difficulty and seizure at work
patient.appearance: Young woman, alert but frightened, slightly disheveled, wearing a waitress uniform. Wedding ring on left hand. She keeps apologizing for the trouble.
patient.backstory: Married for two years, working double shifts as a waitress to save money. Has been eating Sunday dinners with her mother-in-law who prepares traditional dishes including carne de cerdo — sometimes still pink in the middle. She did not want to be rude.
patient.triage_note: Patient seized at restaurant where she works. Coworkers called 911. Speech was slurred on arrival, improved somewhat in transit. No prior seizure history per coworker. Last meal unknown.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Neurocysticercosis (Taenia solium larvae in brain parenchyma)
ground_truth.mechanism: Patient consumed undercooked pork containing Taenia solium cysts over months of Sunday dinners at her mother-in-law home. Oncosphere larvae disseminated hematogenously and lodged in brain parenchyma. Dying larvae triggered focal inflammatory response causing edema, seizures, and progressive neurological decline.
ground_truth.key_insight: The CT shows a ring-enhancing lesion — every trainee anchors to tumor or abscess. The real diagnosis lives in two places: the CBC differential (eosinophilia) and the dietary history (undercooked pork). Both are there from the start. Neither is obvious until you know what you are looking for.

optimal_path.description: Establish timeline: two weeks of worsening headache culminating in seizure with aphasia
Confirm focal deficits: right-sided weakness, expressive aphasia, Babinski positive
CBC with differential — notice the eosinophilia at 8%, above the 1-3% normal range
Ring-enhancing lesion left parietal. Radiologist says tumor vs abscess.
Undercooked pork — Sunday dinners at mother-in-laws every week for two years
Calcified larvae in thigh muscle. Radiologist: consistent with cysticercosis.

narrative_hooks.description: CT ring-enhancing lesion looks exactly like a brain tumor. Radiologist says so. Players anchor here.
narrative_hooks.structural_role: node_06_ct_lesion sets tumor_suspected, unlocking consult and start_treatment as tempting options

narrative_hooks.description: Eosinophilia is in the labs. Most players see WBC normal and move on. The differential tells another story.
narrative_hooks.structural_role: node_04_cbc_results reveals eosinophilia flag that unlocks history_focused and consult

narrative_hooks.description: Diego arrives at T+30. He knows about the Sunday pork meals. He volunteers this if you earn his trust. He leaves at T+120 if ignored.
narrative_hooks.structural_role: node_13_husband_diego provides redundant path to undercooked_pork_exposure via history_focused:family

narrative_hooks.description: Steroids give 60 minutes of false improvement. Maria smiles. Her headache fades. Then the crisis arrives 60 minutes early.
narrative_hooks.structural_role: node_19_steroid_rebound (activated only when steroids are given) accelerates node_09_headache_progression timer by 60 minutes on expire

narrative_hooks.description: MRI takes 45 minutes. Serology takes 120 minutes. The thigh X-ray confirms in 20 minutes if you have earned the hypothesis.
narrative_hooks.structural_role: node_12_xray_confirmation only activates after undercooked_pork_exposure or eosinophilia plus lesion_found

content.narrative_text: Case initializing. Advanced actions gated pending clinical discovery.

Maria recounts the past two weeks carefully. Headaches started gradually — she thought it was stress from double shifts. But they got worse. This morning she was taking a table order when the words stopped making sense. Her arm went stiff. Then nothing until she was in the ambulance. She has never had anything like this. Her speech is slightly halting now, searching for certain words. She is clearly frightened but trying to stay composed.

General exam: Alert, oriented to person and place but slightly slow. Mild expressive hesitancy. No fever. No neck stiffness. Skin clear, no rashes. Abdomen soft, non-tender. Cardiovascular exam unremarkable. You notice she favors her right arm slightly — she has not mentioned it.

Focused neuro exam reveals: Right grip strength 3/5 versus 5/5 on left. Right arm pronator drift positive. Expressive aphasia — she can understand you but searches for words, occasionally substitutes wrong ones. Pupils equal, round, reactive bilaterally. No papilledema on fundoscopic exam. Babinski sign positive on right. Gait mildly ataxic, listing left. Cranial nerves II-XII grossly intact except for the expressive speech deficit.

Complete Blood Count with differential: WBC 9.8 (4.5 to 11.0 normal). Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL. Platelets 224. Differential: Neutrophils 61%, Lymphocytes 27%, Monocytes 4%, Eosinophils 8% (normal 1 to 3%), Basophils 0%. CMP within normal limits. ESR mildly elevated at 28 mm/hr.

nodes.teaching_note: WBC is normal — many players skip the differential. The eosinophilia at 8% is the signal. Parasitic infection, not malignancy.

content.narrative_text: Basic Metabolic Panel: Sodium 138, Potassium 4.1, Chloride 101, Bicarb 24. BUN 14, Creatinine 0.8, Glucose 94. All within normal limits. No electrolyte abnormality to explain altered mental status.

CT Head with contrast: 2.3cm ring-enhancing lesion in the left parietal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema. Midline shift 2mm to the right. Radiologist preliminary read: Ring-enhancing lesion with surrounding edema, left parietal lobe. Differential includes primary brain neoplasm, high-grade glioma versus metastatic lesion versus brain abscess. Recommend MRI brain with and without contrast for further characterization. Recommend neurosurgery consultation.

structured_data.radiologist_impression: Primary brain neoplasm vs. abscess. Recommend MRI.

nodes.teaching_note: The anchoring trap. This looks exactly like a brain tumor. The radiologist says so. Most players will pursue oncology and miss the turn.

content.narrative_text: Maria hesitates. My mother-in-law — she cooks for us every Sunday. She makes traditional things. Carne de cerdo. Sometimes it is still a little pink in the middle. She says that is how her mother always made it. I did not want to say anything. She tries so hard. I have been going there every Sunday for two years since we got married. A pause. I never thought about it.

nodes.teaching_note: The pivot point. Activates only after a clinical reason to ask — eosinophilia, lesion, or Diego tip. Asking at random reveals nothing.

content.narrative_text: Maria is not on any regular medications. She has never had a seizure before. No anticonvulsants, no steroids, no immunosuppressants. She took ibuprofen for the headaches — it helped a little at first, then not at all. No drug allergies. She drinks socially, rarely. No recreational drug use.
Silent deterioration — not directly revealed. Effects manifest through vital sign changes.

MRI Brain with and without contrast: The ring-enhancing lesion shows eccentric internal nodule — the eccentric scolex sign — a small dot within the cyst representing the parasite head. T2 signal shows reactive edema. No satellite lesions. Neuroradiology read: Findings most consistent with a solitary viable cysticercus cyst in the colloidal vesicular stage. Parasite head (scolex) visible. Strongly suggestive of neurocysticercosis. Clinical correlation with exposure history recommended.

structured_data.modality: MRI brain with and without contrast
structured_data.finding: Eccentric scolex sign in ring-enhancing lesion
structured_data.neuroradiology_impression: Solitary cysticercus cyst — strongly suggestive of neurocysticercosis

nodes.teaching_note: Slower path (45-min delay). Highly specific — scolex sign is pathognomonic. By the time MRI results arrive, node_09 has been ticking 45+ minutes.

content.narrative_text: Taenia solium IgG ELISA: POSITIVE. CDC laboratory confirmation. Report: Positive serology in clinical context of ring-enhancing lesion is highly supportive of neurocysticercosis.

structured_data.sensitivity_note: 80-98% for multiple cysts, lower for solitary cyst cases
structured_data.clinical_interpretation: Highly supportive of neurocysticercosis in this clinical context

nodes.teaching_note: Serology takes 120 minutes. Waiting for this before treating is dangerous. Treat on clinical suspicion in high-probability cases.

content.narrative_text: X-ray right thigh (AP and lateral): Two small, calcified ovoid densities measuring 6mm and 8mm in the vastus lateralis muscle belly. No periosteal reaction. Radiologist note: Calcified ovoid densities in muscle tissue consistent with degenerated cysticerci. Findings support diagnosis of systemic cysticercosis.

structured_data.finding: Two calcified ovoid densities in vastus lateralis
structured_data.interpretation: Degenerated cysticerci in muscle tissue — systemic cysticercosis

nodes.teaching_note: Fastest confirmatory test (20-min delay). Only available after building sufficient hypothesis. The X-ray option only appears once earned through clinical reasoning.

content.narrative_text: Diego Santos arrives in the waiting room — Maria's husband. He is agitated, speaking fast, switching between English and Spanish. He demands to know what is happening to his wife. If you approach him with honesty and respect — explain what you know, acknowledge what you do not — he steadies. His eyes fill. She never complains. She was having headaches for two weeks and she did not even tell me. He pauses. My mother cooks for us every Sunday. Maria always eats everything — she does not want to make my mother feel bad. Carne de cerdo, sometimes still pink... is that — could that be related?

nodes.teaching_note: Diego arrives at T+30 and his timer runs 90 minutes — gone by T+120 if not engaged. Engage early. He holds the dietary clue the patient was too polite to share. Arrival is tick-quantized: this node activates on the first engine tick that crosses T+30, so Diego's actual arrival — and therefore his departure — varies with the player's action cadence. Acceptable, but known: consequences wired to this timer (family_alienated) inherit that variance.

content.narrative_text: Maria stops mid-sentence. Her eyes deviate right. Full tonic-clonic seizure — violent, sustained. The monitor alarms cascade: HR spikes to 148. BP crashes to 82/48. SpO2 drops to 86% as she loses airway patency. Your team moves.

nodes.teaching_note: Status epilepticus care: benzodiazepines and airway control end the seizure. emergency_intervention within the 5-minute window deactivates this node — the death clock is removed, vitals recover, and the investigation reopens. But the patient is stabilized, not safe: crisis_managed starts the post-crisis progression clock (node_20).

content.narrative_text: Maria responds to the dexamethasone remarkably quickly. Within the hour, the headache eases. Her speech fluency improves. She smiles for the first time since admission. The swelling around the lesion is temporarily reduced. What everyone in the room does not know yet is that the cytokine cascade keeping the parasites in check is now suppressed.

nodes.teaching_note: Steroids reduce edema and improve symptoms for 60 minutes. Then: immune suppression accelerates progression by 60 minutes. False improvement, catastrophic undercurrent.

content.narrative_text: Maria seizes again — and this time the interventions do not hold. Intracranial pressure rises beyond what the brain can compensate for. Herniation follows. Despite everything your team does, time of death is called. She was 28 years old. Her husband is in the waiting room.

You start Maria on albendazole 400mg BD with a meal, alongside an anticonvulsant for seizure prophylaxis. You counsel her on what to expect: nausea, headache, possible fever — the inflammation that comes with the parasite dying. She absorbs it carefully. If it gets rid of whatever is in my head, I will take it. Over the following hours, the progression stops. Vitals stabilize. She asks to call Diego.

Clinical suspicion for neurocysticercosis now sufficient for empirical antiparasitic treatment: eosinophilia and ring-enhancing lesion together raise the probability high enough to justify commitment without awaiting confirmatory imaging or serology.

nodes.teaching_note: Eosinophilia plus ring-enhancing lesion is suspicion-grade evidence for neurocysticercosis. Committing to albendazole at this point is clinically defensible — the Good tier. Waiting for MRI scolex sign or serology is cautious and earns Optimal.

content.narrative_text: Beneath the apparent improvement, the dexamethasone has suppressed the immune response that was holding the parasites in check. The inflammation quiets. The cysticerci flourish. The progression accelerates, unseen.

nodes.teaching_note: The steroid rebound. Sixty minutes after dexamethasone is given, immune suppression accelerates the progression timeline by 60 minutes — the false improvement window is exactly the rebound delay. Activates only when steroids are actually administered.

content.narrative_text: Silent post-crisis deterioration — not directly revealed. The seizure is over but the parasites are not. Effects manifest through vital sign changes.

nodes.teaching_note: The re-arm. Managing the seizure buys 90 minutes, not safety — untreated neurocysticercosis progresses to a second crisis. The stabilized window is the player's last chance to commit to treatment. Non-diegetic by design: the player reads it from the vitals, exactly like node_09.

content.narrative_text: It happens again — faster this time. Maria's head turns, her eyes deviate right, and the seizure takes her whole body. The monitor alarms are worse than before: HR 152. BP 78/44. SpO2 falling through 84%. The team looks at you. Whatever was building underneath the last ninety minutes has arrived.

nodes.teaching_note: The mechanic does not lie the second time: emergency_intervention rescues this crisis exactly as it rescued the first. A distinct node rather than a reactivation of node_14 — the second seizure on an untreated brain is a different, worse event, and its vitals say so. After a second rescue there is no third clock; the untreated run runs out at T+360 into the fallthrough tier.

tiers.narrative: Maria recovers fully. The parasitic infection is identified and treated before the crisis can develop. Diego is informed and involved — he understands what happened, and he will quietly talk to his mother about the pork. Maria returns to work within weeks. She sends a thank-you note.

Maria recovers, but the delay caused additional neurological trauma. She has residual word-finding difficulty that improves slowly over months. The parasites are treated. The outcome is positive — but she carries the consequences of a late diagnosis.

Maria survives. Treatment was eventually correct, but the path there caused lasting harm — a diagnosis that came late, or a husband who left the waiting room believing nobody would talk to him. She has permanent neurological sequelae. This was preventable.
Maria died. The diagnosis was not reached in time, or the wrong treatment accelerated the deterioration past the point of recovery. She was 28 years old.

The shift ends with Maria still in the department — alive, deteriorating, undiagnosed. Six hours, and the answer was in her chart and in her family the whole time. She is transferred to the ICU under a working diagnosis that is wrong. What happens next happens without you.

harmful_actions.description: Started high-dose steroids (dexamethasone) for presumed tumor edema or vasculitis
harmful_actions.penalty_note: Steroids suppress immune response, allow the parasite to flourish, and accelerate the progression timeline by 60 minutes. The initial improvement is a trap.

end_conditions.description: Patient dies from untreated or mismanaged neurocysticercosis
Case time limit reached — 6 hours simulated
Correct antiparasitic treatment initiated — case can resolve
